metadata.title: High-Performance Computing Identity and Access

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for ensuring correct identification, authentication, and authorization of users, workloads, and schedulers in shared high-performance computing environments.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: HPC identity systems, batch schedulers, job submission interfaces, and non-interactive execution contexts.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for governing identity, job attribution, and access control in scheduler-mediated HPC platforms.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: HPC identity and access assumptions build on foundational trust in shared HPC platforms.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Credential access risks associated with shared login nodes, job submission mechanisms, or scheduler services.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Privilege escalation through misuse of scheduler roles or misattributed job execution.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Defense evasion by executing jobs under incorrect or unintended identities.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid accounts to submit or execute unauthorized HPC jobs.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation via scheduler or identity misconfiguration.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Privileged access management for HPC administrators, schedulers, and service accounts.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Strong authentication mechanisms for interactive and non-interactive HPC access.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Separation of duties between users, schedulers, and platform administrators.

metadata.remarks: High-Performance Computing Identity and Access defines the trust properties required to correctly attribute, authorize, and constrain users and workloads in scheduler-driven HPC environments. This pattern recognizes that HPC systems frequently rely on non-interactive execution contexts and shared login infrastructure, making identity assurance and role separation critical.

components.title: Job Identity Attribution
components.description: Ensures that HPC jobs are unambiguously attributed to the correct initiating identity.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Each job execution is associated with an accountable user or service identity.

components.title: Scheduler Access Control
components.description: Restricts who may submit, modify, or control jobs through the HPC scheduler.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Access to scheduler functions is limited to authorized identities and roles.

components.title: Role Separation and Delegation
components.description: Separates user, administrator, and scheduler roles to prevent inappropriate privilege overlap.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Distinct roles and delegation boundaries prevent unauthorized escalation or misuse.
